question: Should OpenClaw core support ordered multi-document configuration as a public Gateway startup contract, and is this startup-only read-only model the intended boundary?
rationale: The PR creates a new operator-facing configuration and CLI mode while its linked architecture RFC remains open, so implementation quality cannot determine long-term product acceptance.

options.title: RFC-first sponsorship
options.body: Keep the draft open but pause implementation acceptance until the RFC defines the supported precedence, ownership, mutation, reload, and upgrade contract.

options.title: Sponsor the narrow mode
options.body: Approve the startup-only read-only contract, then require a current-main rebase, path-scoped ownership, and live proof before merge.

options.title: Keep composition external
options.body: Continue requiring hosts to materialize one canonical validated OpenClaw configuration before Gateway startup.

recommendation.title: RFC-first sponsorship
recommendation.body: Keep the draft open but pause implementation acceptance until the RFC defines the supported precedence, ownership, mutation, reload, and upgrade contract.

likelyOwner.reason: This is the best available repository-level owner for confirming whether the new public configuration mode belongs in core.
